about.title: South Gate Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription:
Most people in South Gate never expect to second-guess their doctor. You visit a clinic off Firestone Boulevard, or you are admitted after a collision on Imperial Highway, and you trust the people in scrubs to get it right. Usually they do. Sometimes they do not, and the difference between a hard outcome and a preventable one is exactly where medical malpractice law begins.

California's MICRA framework governs these claims. In plain terms, you generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file. Before a lawsuit is filed, a 90-day notice must go to each provider involved. Nearly every case also needs a qualified medical expert to explain what a careful provider would have done differently. A bad result, by itself, is not malpractice.

LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that links South Gate residents in Los Angeles County with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why South Gate Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines that start before you know it
items.desc: MICRA generally allows one year from discovery and never more than three years from the injury. An attorney can pin down which date applies to you before options close.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: California requires written notice to each provider 90 days before suit. Getting that step wrong can cost time you may not have, so it pays to have someone who does it routinely.

items.title: Experts and the damages cap explained plainly
items.desc: Almost every malpractice case needs a qualified medical expert, and non-economic damages are subject to a statutory cap that rises each year. The attorney you are matched with can walk you through both without jargon.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Firestone Boulevard and my hospital care made things worse. Is that a car accident case or a malpractice case?
items.answer: It can be both, and they are handled differently. The collision claim runs against the driver and their insurer, while a separate malpractice claim may exist if a provider's care fell below the accepted standard. With 419 injury collisions recorded in South Gate in 2025, this overlap is not unusual, and an attorney can evaluate whether each piece stands on its own.

items.question: My surgery did not turn out the way I hoped. Does that mean I have a case?
items.answer: Not by itself. Medicine carries real risk, and a disappointing result is not the same as negligence. What matters is whether a reasonably careful provider would have acted differently, and that question is nearly always answered by a qualified medical expert reviewing your records.
